summary: Ru thin films were grown on TiO2, Al2O3, HfO2, ZrO2, and SiO2/Si substrates using atomic layer deposition from 1-ethyl-1'-methyl-ruthenocene and oxygen. The films were characterized for their structure, morphology, and conductivity. The growth was studied at temperatures ranging from 250 to 325 °C, with the highest conductivity observed at 275 °C. The films were found to be metallic with hexagonal structure and no Ru oxide was detected inside the films. The conductivity and roughness of the films increased with the number of deposition cycles.
evidence: Ru thin films were grown on TiO2, Al2O3, HfO2, ZrO2, and SiO2/Si substrates using atomic layer deposition from 1-ethyl-1'-methyl-ruthenocene and oxygen. The growth of Ru was obtained and characterized at temperatures ranging from 250 to 325 °C. The films were found to be metallic with hexagonal structure and no Ru oxide was detected inside the films. The conductivity of the films depended somewhat on the deposition cycle time parameters and, expectedly, more strongly on the amount of deposition cycles. Increase in the deposition temperature of underlying metal oxide films increased the conductivity of Ru layers.
